stem: A CPU-bound Lambda function currently runs at 256 MB and finishes slowly, and before assuming the smallest memory setting is cheapest, the team wants to know whether raising memory would lower the total cost per invocation.

choices.text: Enable reserved concurrency to guarantee available capacity
Test several higher memory settings against real traffic
Enable provisioned concurrency to remove cold starts
Repackage the function as a container image at the same memory setting

rationale: Because CPU scales with memory, testing several higher memory values against real traffic reveals whether a shorter billed duration outweighs the higher per-millisecond price, which is exactly how to check whether raising memory lowers total cost. Reserved concurrency only sets how many invocations can run at once; it does not change execution speed or cost per invocation. Provisioned concurrency removes cold-start latency for already-running capacity, but it does not address whether raising memory would speed up and cheapen an already-warm invocation. Repackaging as a container image changes how the function is deployed, not its CPU allocation, so it does not answer the memory-versus-cost question at all.
